aboutAuthor: William J. O'Neil founded Investor's Business Daily and studied 100 years of super winners to codify CAN SLIM — Current earnings, Annual growth, New products, Supply demand, Leaders, Institutional sponsorship, Market direction.

points.heading: Winners leave empirical footprints
points.body: 54 percent quarterly earnings growth, new highs off proper bases, and volume spikes repeat across a century of super winners that rose 300 percent plus, providing a training set more useful than studying losers.

points.heading: Buy leaders at new highs off proper bases
points.body: Cup-with-handle depth fifteen to thirty percent and handle five to fifteen on low volume with volume 1.5 times average at breakout in stage one or two predicts success; laggard value traps cheap for a reason.

points.heading: C and A gate with acceleration
points.body: Quarterly eighteen percent minimum accelerating with sales twenty-five percent plus, and annual twenty-five percent three-year with margin expansion, must both pass before chart or story matters.

points.heading: Supply, sponsors, and market tide
points.body: Low float, accumulation Rating A, and 10-30 rising sponsors confirm demand, but even perfect leader fails seventy-five percent without uptrend market confirmed by follow-through and distribution counts.

points.heading: Sell discipline makes expectancy
points.body: Cut every loss at seven to eight percent without discussion and hold power stocks eight weeks when up twenty percent in three weeks to let winners reach forty and cover many small losses.

points.heading: System over prediction
points.body: Six to eight leaders concentrated, no margin, theme rotation via 197 groups, and daily fifteen-minute IBD routine of SmartSelect and Market Pulse replaces forecasting with process.

insights: AAII 1998-2009 independent study where CAN SLIM delivered 2,763 percent versus S&P 3.3 percent annually via process adherence.
Cup-with-handle breakout on volume 280 percent of average at Xerox in 1963 that ran 400 percent, the textbook base that repeats.
Eight percent mechanical stop where 8 percent loss needs 8.7 percent to recover but 50 percent needs 100, the math of survival.
conclusion: How to Make Money in Stocks turns a century of winners into a gated CAN SLIM system where earnings, newness, leader charts, and market timing compound via ruthless eight percent stops and eight-week winner holds.
